publication: No staging, commits, pushes, remote issues or releases performed.
scope: Twenty selected backlog stories for isolated tools, document OCR/review, connector safety, training export, SDK and release evidence.

architecture.tool_isolation: WASI with read-only explicit inputs and process budgets; arbitrary native subprocess execution rejected because cwd/env filtering is not an OS sandbox.
architecture.oauth_host: Shared Python host-owned loopback helper instead of duplicated Rust authorization logic; registration remains trusted-host-only.
architecture.design: Existing approved Veya Public Sans/Phosphor workspace and contextual source drawer; no new generic dashboard or sidebar redesign.

limitations: Stories remain in_review; implementation commits and formal prerequisite acceptance are pending user review.

GitHub CI has not run these local changes. Repository protection visibility was unknown.

stories.assessment: Approved WASI modules execute through ToolBinding/ToolExecutor with fuel, memory, deadline, stdout and explicit read-only input limits. Native executables are unsupported.
Optional local RapidOCR/PDFium extraction recognizes a real raster invoice and returns normalized regions/confidence. OCR model hashes are verified before load; five scanned pages maximum.

Typed invoice header review is wired Angular -> Go -> Python. Original values, evidence regions, corrections, reviewer, note and revisions survive restart; missing/conflicting values require explicit input.

Document workers now cap output while reading and run with a minimal environment in disposable directories. Malformed parser input does not prevent the next document; untrusted instructions remain source text.

MCP JSON/HTTP client negotiates pinned 2025-11-25, discovers bounded catalogs and requires host-approved typed mappings. Server instructions/annotations cannot add permissions. SSE, newer protocols and dynamic tools are explicitly unsupported.

Host-owned numeric-loopback authorization-code PKCE helper binds state, issuer, redirect and scopes; state is durable and single-use, tokens use vault references. Verified with a real loopback callback and synthetic provider. No live provider registration/account consent claimed.
Explicit synthetic drive adapter lists only a granted folder, imports stable remote identities/revisions through document intake and links retained evidence. Removal denies later retrieval.
Synthetic ticket create/update binding uses exact approvals and durable operation fingerprints. A simulated timeout after commit reconciles to one verified ticket ID; later writes fail after removal.
Revision-fenced token refresh preserves exact scopes and rotates vault references. Scope changes require reauthorization; concurrent removal wins and cannot resurrect a connection.

Connector removal disables future calls before credential cleanup, records audit evidence, and revokes connector document retrieval without deleting source bytes. Safe status/removal commands exposed through Go and the SDK.

TRL conversational export composes existing review, consent, scrubbing, deduplication and lineage controls. Actual Qwen tokenizer/template round-trip passed; mismatched tokenizer identity, truncation, incomplete tools and revoked sources fail closed. No training or quality promotion claimed.

Explicit relative file grants reject traversal/link escapes and bound reads. MCP/OAuth HTTPS transport rejects private/mixed DNS resolutions, connects to the approved numeric address with original TLS hostname, and does not follow credential-bearing redirects.

Host-approved plugin identity pins module digest, version and capabilities; changed bytes are quarantined before execution and unsupported native formats cannot load. Integration test exercises the normal policy gateway.
Authenticated API and real Go SDK regressions reject forged tenant/workspace/approval/budget fields, unknown privileged operations and invalid credentials without task writes.
Bounded artifact verification checks immutable bytes against explicit SHA-256; mismatches are quarantined before plugin/OCR loading. Valid artifacts are reusable.

Adversarial checks cover output floods, deadlines, repeated invalid credentials, oversized bodies and admission saturation/cancellation recovery. Existing event and telemetry bounds also run in the full suite.

Generic artifact manifest records source commit, dirty state, locked input hashes, artifact checksums, CycloneDX dependency inventory and unsigned in-toto provenance. Platform and native workflows consume it with read-only permissions and no signing/publishing credentials. No container build, installed installer QA or signed attestation claimed.

Read-only repository audit evaluates required checks, review count, administrator enforcement and protected environments. Missing visibility is unknown. The actual audit returned unknown protection/environment status and remains noncompliant; no remote setting changed.

Installable local Python SDK starts, observes, executes and cancels through authenticated Go commands, with bounded transport and no automatic write retries or approval bypass. Tested against the real Go/Python process.
Credential-free contributor command runs eight adapter success/fault/permission contracts against explicit synthetic fixtures and reports unsupported production/native capabilities.
